routes.title: Where are you moving?
routes.lead: Pick a source and a destination. Every figure comes from a real run.
routes.same: Z-Move moves workloads between clouds and between Zadara regions. Inside a single AWS or Azure account, use the provider's own tools.
routes.none: This route is not supported yet. Tell us if you need it.

zadara>zadara.how: Relay. An export worker reads the source, an import worker writes the destination, and the disks stream between them in memory, over TLS.
zadara>zadara.result: An image in the destination region, ready to launch.
zadara>zadara.note: Production firewall VM, moved between two Zadara regions.
zadara>zadara.os: Nothing to adapt: the same platform on both sides.
zadara>zadara.boot: Available. The test VM has to answer on SSH, RDP, HTTPS or HTTP.

aws>zadara.how: Relay. A worker in AWS reads an EBS snapshot and streams it to an import worker in Zadara.
aws>zadara.result: A Zadara image, ready to launch.
aws>zadara.note: Validation run, AWS US East to Zadara, with boot test.
aws>zadara.os: Linux boots as it is: the VirtIO drivers ship with the kernel. For Windows, check the VirtIO drivers before the cutover.

zadara>aws.how: Relay. A worker in Zadara streams the disks to an import worker in AWS.
zadara>aws.result: An AMI registered with ENA, ready for current instance types.
zadara>aws.note: Validation run, Zadara to AWS US East.
zadara>aws.os: Linux and Windows are copied block by block, as they are.

azure>zadara.how: Direct. One worker in Zadara reads the Azure snapshot itself, with nothing in the middle.
azure>zadara.result: A Zadara image, with the system already adapted.
azure>zadara.note: Validation run, Azure East US to Zadara, Ubuntu 24.04.
azure>zadara.os: Adapted automatically in 3 s: cloud-init, network (netplan), Azure agent and fstab.

zadara>azure.how: Direct upload. Only the parts of each disk that hold data are sent.
zadara>azure.result: An Azure managed disk (Standard SSD). You create the VM from it in the Azure portal.
zadara>azure.note: Validation run, Zadara to Azure East US, upload at 166 MB/s.
zadara>azure.os: Adapted for Azure, with a check for the Hyper-V drivers.
zadara>azure.boot: Not yet for Azure destinations. Start the VM in the portal to confirm.

sec.title: Ready for your security review.
sec.lead: The questions your security team will ask, answered up front.

items.d: Z-Move only reads snapshots through the cloud APIs. The source is never stopped or changed, so rolling back means carrying on with it.
Cloud credentials are encrypted at rest, never written to logs, and deleted 30 days after the job ends.
Each temporary worker gets a token valid only for its job, opens no inbound ports and is destroyed at the end.
TLS on every hop. Relayed disks stream in memory and are never written to disk. Azure routes go straight between the clouds.
Administrators sign in with a second factor. Every change is recorded: who, what, when and from where.

items.t: Your own cloud, if you prefer
items.d: Run Z-Move inside your own infrastructure and keep every byte there.

items.q: Do I need to install anything in my VMs?
items.a: No. Z-Move works with snapshots and volumes through the cloud APIs, using temporary workers that it creates and removes itself.

items.q: How much downtime should I plan for?
items.a: Z-Move copies a snapshot, so the source keeps running. For a consistent copy of a busy application, stop the application or the VM before the snapshot, and the downtime becomes the copy time of that VM. Between Zadara regions, replication keeps a standby up to date for shorter windows.
Linux and Windows. Disks are copied block by block, so the system moves as it is. Linux VMs from Azure are adapted automatically. For Windows, check the destination's drivers before the cutover.

items.q: Does my data pass through your servers?
items.a: On Zadara ↔ Zadara and AWS ↔ Zadara routes, disks stream through the Z-Move relay over TLS, in memory, and are never written to disk. Azure routes go straight between the clouds. With a private deployment, everything stays in your infrastructure.

items.q: What happens if a migration fails?
items.a: The job log shows where and why. Workers are cleaned up and you retry from the same screen; disks already copied are reused and not billed again. The source is never touched, so a failure never puts it at risk.

items.q: Can I replicate or export instead of migrating?
items.a: Yes. Replication keeps a standby VM in another Zadara region in sync, every 30 minutes up to every 24 hours, with failover from the dashboard. Export writes a VM's disks as qcow2 or VHD to your own S3 bucket.

sec.title: Pronto para a sua revisão de segurança.
sec.lead: As perguntas que a sua equipa de segurança vai fazer, respondidas à partida.

items.d: O Z-Move só lê snapshots pelas APIs da cloud. A origem nunca é parada nem alterada, por isso voltar atrás é continuar com ela.
As credenciais das clouds ficam cifradas, nunca vão para os logs e são apagadas 30 dias depois do fim do job.
Cada worker temporário recebe um token válido só para o seu job, não abre portas de entrada e é destruído no fim.

Os administradores entram com um segundo factor. Cada alteração fica registada: quem, o quê, quando e de onde.
Instale o Z-Move na sua própria infraestrutura e mantenha lá cada byte.

items.q: Tenho de instalar alguma coisa nas VMs?
items.a: Não. O Z-Move trabalha com snapshots e volumes pelas APIs das clouds, com workers temporários que cria e remove sozinho.

items.q: Quanto tempo de paragem devo prever?
items.a: O Z-Move copia um snapshot, por isso a origem continua a funcionar. Para uma cópia consistente de uma aplicação com muita escrita, pare a aplicação ou a VM antes do snapshot, e a paragem passa a ser o tempo de cópia dessa VM. Entre regiões Zadara, a replicação mantém uma VM de reserva actualizada para janelas mais curtas.

Linux e Windows. Os discos são copiados bloco a bloco, por isso o sistema muda tal como está. As VMs Linux vindas do Azure são adaptadas automaticamente. Em Windows, confirme os drivers do destino antes da mudança.

items.q: Os meus dados passam pelos vossos servidores?
items.a: Nas rotas Zadara ↔ Zadara e AWS ↔ Zadara, os discos passam pelo relay do Z-Move, por TLS, em memória, e nunca são escritos em disco. As rotas Azure vão directamente entre as clouds. Com uma instalação privada, tudo fica na sua infraestrutura.

O log do job mostra onde e porquê. Os workers são limpos e repete no mesmo ecrã; os discos já copiados são reaproveitados e não voltam a ser cobrados. A origem nunca é tocada, por isso uma falha nunca a põe em risco.

items.q: Posso replicar ou exportar em vez de migrar?
items.a: Sim. A replicação mantém uma VM de reserva sincronizada noutra região Zadara, de 30 em 30 minutos até de 24 em 24 horas, com failover no painel. A exportação escreve os discos de uma VM em qcow2 ou VHD no seu próprio bucket S3.
